properties.name: Amundsen Ridges
properties.historia: Named after the Norwegian Polar explorer Roald Amundsen 1872-1928, who led the expedition that first reached the South Pole in 1911. He also was the first to fly over the North Pole on an airship in 1926.

properties.name: JOIDES Basin

properties.name: Marie Byrd Canyon

properties.historia: Named after the wife of American Admiral Richard Byrd, leader 1928 expedition to Bay of Whales.

properties.name: Prestrud Bank

properties.name: Ross Canyon

properties.name: Scott Canyon

properties.name: Wild Canyon

properties.name: Bruce Ridge
properties.historia: Named after William Spiers Bruce, leader of the Scottish national (Scotia) expedition to the Weddell Sea 1903-1904.

properties.name: Endurance Canyon
properties.historia: Named after Sir Ernest Shackleton's ship which was crushed by the Antarctic ice in November 1915.

properties.name: Molyneux Canyon
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Molyneux Sea Channel
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Nachtigaller Shoal
properties.historia: The name "Nachtigaller" is a figure from a series of novels written by W. Moers. In the novels, Prof. Nachtigaller dedicates his life to the research of the mysteries of the world. In order to do so, he visits the most remote areas of the earth. He has special preference for dark and hostile places.
properties.proponente: Boris Dorschel, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Adare Basin
properties.historia: Named from the adjacent feature on land, Cape Adare.
properties.proponente: Fred J. Davey, Institute of Geological & Nuclear Sciences, New Zealand

properties.name: Akademik Fedorov Canyon
properties.historia: Named after the Soviet Research Ship "Akademik Fedorov" which worked in this area in 1989.
properties.proponente: Heinrich Hinze, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Althoff Seamount
properties.historia: Named after Friedrich Althoff (1839-1909), German lawyer and patron of the 1899 Valdivia Expedition led by Carl Chun.
properties.proponente: Sonja Guetz, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Anashkin Seamount
properties.historia: Named after Aleksey Alekseyevich Anashkin (1914-1987), a Russian hydrographer for the Pacific Fleet, at HDNO. He conducted hydrographic research in the Far East seas.
properties.proponente: Department of Navigation and Oceanography (DNO), Russia

properties.name: Andenes Knoll
properties.historia: Named after the Norwegian Research Vessel "Andenes" which carried out geophysical research in this part of the Weddell Sea.
properties.proponente: Heinrich Hinze, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Anderle Knoll
properties.historia: Named after Richard J. Anderle (1926-1994), an expert of the dynamic geodesy methods of positioning by satellite.
properties.proponente: Heinrich Hinze, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Andrew Bain Fracture Zone
properties.historia: Named after Andrew Geddes Bain ("Father of South African Geology": A. du Toit), a mid-1800's field geologist-mapmaker-stratigrapher who noted similarities between fossil plants of Falklands-South Africa-Australia, in a sense anticipating Gondwanaland.
properties.proponente: Robert L. Fisher, Scripps Institution of Oceanography (SIO), USA; and Christopher J. H. Hartnady, University of Cape Town (UCT), South Africa

properties.name: Anna de Koningh Seamount
properties.historia: Named after Anna De Koningh, a Bengalese who arrived at the Cape in 1655 in early childhood, and became a successful vegetable trader in Cape Town. She married a white settler in 1669 and a Dutch East India company soldier, Olof Bergh, between 1676 and 1687. After eventful and controversial careers, Bergh and wife became by 1715 the "most considerable landowners" of all the prospering officials in a free-booting era.
properties.proponente: Hugh W. Bergh, Wits Bernard Price Institute (BPI), South Africa; and Robert L. Fisher, Scripps Institution of Oceanography (SIO), USA

properties.name: Anschütz-Kämpfe Trough
properties.historia: Named after Herman Anschütz-Kämpfe (1872-1931) who suggested a submarine research expedition below the polar sea ice in 1901.
properties.proponente: Heinrich Hinze, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Antarctic Canyon
properties.historia: Most likely named after the Norwegian whaler "Antarctic" sent out in 1984-1995 to investigate reports of commercially profitable whales.

properties.name: Antipodes Fracture Zone
properties.historia: Named from the nearby Antipodes Islands, New Zealand.
properties.proponente: Steven C. Cande, Scripps Institution of Oceanography (SIO), USA

properties.name: Atka Bank
properties.historia: Named after the U.S. vessel "Atka" which operated in this area and anchored in Atka Bay in 1956.
properties.proponente: Heinrich Hinze, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Austaasen Bank
properties.historia: "Austaasen" is Norwegian for "Eastern Hill" (elevation), i.e. the elevation east of the former Maudheim research station.
properties.proponente: Heinrich Hinze, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Australian-Antarctic Discordance
properties.historia: Named from its location between Australia and Antarctica.
properties.proponente: Robin K. H. Falconer, Institute of Geological and Nuclear Sciences (GNS Science), New Zealand

properties.name: Baeyer Canyon
properties.historia: Named after Johann Jacob Baeyer (1794-1885) who initiated the European longitude measuring project "Europäische Gradmessung". Baeyer put forward visionary ideas concerning international co-operation in technical science.
properties.proponente: Heinrich Hinze, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Balleny Seamount
properties.historia: Named after the adjacent Balleny Islands.

properties.name: Barsukov Seamount
properties.historia: Named after the Russian Academician B. L. Barsukov (1928-1992), geochemist, former director of Vernadsky Institute of Geochemistry, Moscow.
properties.proponente: Gleb B. Udintsev, Institute of Oceanology of the Russian Academy of Sciences (IO RAS)

properties.name: Behaim Seamount
properties.historia: Named after Martin Behaim (1459-1507), German cosmographer and navigator. He constructed the first terrestrial globe in 1492.
properties.proponente: Heinrich Hinze, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Behm Bank
properties.historia: Named after Alexander Behm (1880-1952), inventor of an echo-sounding apparatus in 1912/13.
properties.proponente: Heinrich Hinze, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Berkner Bank
properties.historia: Named from the nearby Berkner Island, Antarctica, which itself was named after Lloyd V. Berkner, American physicist and an engineer with the Byrd Antarctic Expedition, 1928-1930.

properties.name: Bruns Knoll
properties.historia: Named after Heinrich Bruns (1848-1919) who developed the three-dimensional coordinate system for astronomy and mathematics, and a global network of terrestrial fixed points.
properties.proponente: Heinrich Hinze, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Brunt Basin
properties.historia: Named from the associated "Brunt Ice Shelf", which was named after David Brunt, Physical Secretary of the British Royal Society.
properties.proponente: Heinrich Hinze, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Bullard Fracture Zone
properties.historia: Named after Sir Edward Bullard (1907-1980), British physicist renowned for magnetic field studies, theory and measurement of heat flow in oceanic regions, and tectonic reconstructions.
properties.proponente: Lawrence A. Lawver, University of Texas at Austin, USA

properties.name: Bungenstock Plateau
properties.historia: Named after Prof. Dr. Herwald Bungenstock, German geologist and geophysicist, who carried out scientific work in the Red Sea and Pacific Ocean, with R/V Valdivia and R/V Sonne. He was the initiator of post-war Marine and Polar Research in Germany and an adviser for Polar and Marine Research to the Minister for Research and Technology (1978-1991). He died in July 1998.
properties.proponente: Hans Werner Schenke, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Campbell Escarpment
properties.historia: Named in association with the nearby Campbell Plateau, of which this feature clearly defines the eastern margin. Campbell Plateau was itself named from the adjacent Campbell Island, New Zealand.
properties.proponente: Lionel Carter, National Institute of Water and Atmospheric Research (NIWA), New Zealand

properties.name: Central Basin
properties.historia: Named from its geographical position, as this feature is located midway between Adare Basin and Iselin Bank and approximately central along the Ross Sea margin. It also lies approximately on the northern extension of a geological rift under the continental shelf called Central Trough.
properties.proponente: Fred J. Davey, Institute of Geological & Nuclear Sciences, New Zealand

properties.name: Charcot Fan
properties.historia: Named after Dr. Jean Charcot, leader of French expedition to west coast Graham Land (1903-1905).

properties.name: Charcot Ridge
properties.historia: Presumably named after French R/V "Jean Charcot". The name itself comes from Dr. Jean Charcot, leader of French expedition to west coast Graham Land (1903-1905).

properties.name: Chun Spur

properties.descubridor: U.S. oceanographic research vessel "Eltanin"; and French research and supply vessel "Marion Dufresne"
properties.proponente: Robert L. Fisher, Scripps Institution of Oceanography (SIO), USA

properties.name: Colbeck Basin
properties.historia: Named after William Colbeck who was with Borchgrevink, and subsequently was in command of "Morning", the relief ship sent out to find "Discovery" 1902-1903.

properties.name: Coral Bank
properties.historia: Named from the many samples of spectacular large red gorgonian "soft corals" that have been collected from this bank during recent fishery research.
properties.proponente: J. J. Doyle, Australian Hydrographic Service (AHS)

properties.name: Crary Fan
properties.historia: Named after Albert P. Crary (1911-1987), American geophysicist. Chief Scientist, Office of Antarctic Programs, Director Division of Environmental Sciences, then Division of Earth Sciences, National Science Foundation, USA.
properties.proponente: Heinrich Hinze, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Da Vinci Bank

properties.name: Eötvös Escarpment
properties.historia: Named after Dr. Lóránd Eötvös (1848-1919), a Hungarian professional scientist in experimental physics and geophysics. Dr. Eötvös invented the Eötvös balance instrument and showed that, to a high degree of accuracy, gravitational mass and inertial mass are equivalent. Because the instrument is very sensitive and not suitable for data mass production, it was replaced by the gravimeter. However, the Eötvös balance is still used today for special geodetic and geophysical applications. Eötvös founded the Hungarian Society for Mathematics in 1885, and was active in improving educational standards in Hungary. What was once the Péter Pázmány University in Budapest is now known as the Lóránd Eötvös University.
properties.proponente: Heinrich Hinze, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Herrmann Canyon
properties.historia: Named after Dr. Ernst Herrmann (1895-1970), the geologist and geographer for the 3rd German Antarctic Expedition aboard the M.V. Schwabenland (December 1938-April 1939). He obtained a PhD in Geology from the university in Berlin, then became a voluntary teaching assistant at the Mineralogical and Petrographic Institute in Berlin. He had strong polar interests and organised geological and glaciological expeditions to Sweden, Norway and Iceland between 1924 and 1934. In summer 1938 he used the new slow-flying Fieseler Storch aircraft to undertake a photographic exploration of the geography of Svalbard, publishing a travel report as a popular book, and making the first coloured aerial movie in the Arctic. Herrmann also had a special interest in volcanoes, and was appointed a member of the Santorin-Expedition to investigate the eruption of one the volcanoes of the Mediterranean island of Santorini, in 1925-1926. He later participated in expeditions to volcanoes in Iceland and Italy (in 1932, 1936, 1937, and 1939). Herrmann described himself as a teacher and polar researcher. Having been wounded during the first World War, he was exempt from military service in the second. As a member of the Freemasons he was not a member of the National Socialist Party and as a consequence was never promoted as teacher. In addition to teaching, he published books and papers and gave lectures and radio broadcasts on geology and geography. His later books included "Die Pole der Erde" (The Poles of the Earth; 1950) and "Die Werkstatt Vulkane" (The Volcano Workshop; 1963). In 1947 he became docent of geography in Bederkesa and at the teacher training college in Celle, and later in Osnabrück.
properties.proponente: Colin Summerhayes, Scott Polar Research Institute, UK

properties.name: Kraul Canyon
properties.historia: Named after the German Captain Otto Kraul (1892-1972), the ice pilot on the MV "Schwabenland" during the 3rd German Antarctic Expedition (December 1938-April 1939). He was a seasoned polar whaler - 47 years old - who had sailed most of the seven seas. The season before (1937/1938) he had been Fangleiter (whaling manager) on the German whaling ship "Jan Wellem" in the Antarctic. Kraul started his career in whaling as a worker at the whaling station of the Compania Argentina de Pesca in Grytviken during World War I. Then he became seaman on a whale catcher, was promoted pilot, and later in the 1920s sometimes held the well-paid position of whale shooter. In 1928 he earned his captain's ticket. Theoretical learning was not his strong point, and in his final examination he failed in physics, meteorology and oceanography, passing the other subjects with the lowest possible grades. Kraul's strengths were practical, and he could tell the most exciting stories about his experiences. His life story up to and including his experiences on the "Schwabenland" was published as: Kraul, O., 1939, Käpt'n Kraul Erzählt. F. A. Herbig, Berlin, 240 pp. Kraul's experience of sailing steel hulled ships unprotected against ice in icy seas was invaluable to Ritscher, the leader of the expedition, and got the ship out of some difficult situations when the ship was manoeuvring among sea ice close to the coast. Avoiding ice was imperative as the main task of the expedition was to launch aerial survey aircraft (seaplanes) to map Dronning Maud Land for the first time (the major achievement of the expedition). The "Schwabenland" was a catapult ship borrowed from Lufthansa who used it for the South America mail run. But the returning seaplanes had to land on water - hence the need to avoid sea ice at all costs. On one occasion "Schwabenland" was nearly crushed by sea ice, until Kraul found the leads that would enable her to escape. "Schwabenland" made major bathymetric discoveries including undertaking the first N-S echo-sounding transect down the mid-Atlantic Ridge in the S Atlantic, and one of the first echo-sounding crossings of the ridge, complementing the set made by "Meteor" in the 1920s. It also unwittingly discovered the Enderby and Weddell Abyssal Plains. The echo-sounding profiles were published in 1958 as a contribution to the IGY.

properties.name: Kurentsova Seamount
properties.historia: Named after Natasha Kurentsova (1938-2010), former Senior scientist at the Vernadsky Institute of Geochemistry and Analytical Chemistry (GEOCHI). She obtained geological education at the Far Eastern Polytechnic Institute, Vladivostok, and finished her academic training in 1960. She worked later at the Pacific division of the Shirshov Institute of Oceanology (since 1968, the Pacific Oceanology Institute), in Vladivostok, and participated in a number of seagoing expeditions as marine geologist. In 1964-1965 Natasha attended the 36th cruise of "Vitjaz" as petrologist, and contributed to the first discovery of the upper mantle rocks outcrops, dredged in the rift zone of the Karlsberg Ridge (NW-branch of the Mid-Ocean Ridge system in the Indian Ocean). She actively collaborated in studies of the mid-oceanic ridges of the Atlantic, Indian Ocean and Pacific. In 1971 she moved to the laboratory of Geomorphology and Tectonics at the Shirshov Institute of Oceanology, Moscow. She joined the 49th cruise of "Vitjaz" in the West Pacific, led the dredging program in the newly discovered Vitjaz Trench (north of the North Fiji Basin) and made first discoveries of upper mantle rocks outcrops. From 1992, she worked in the laboratory for Geomorphology and Tectonics of the Ocean Floor at GEOCHI. She attended the 21st and 29th cruises of R/V "Akademik Boris Petrov" and on several Antarctic expeditions of the German RV "Polarstern" in the Atlantic and Pacific Sectors of the Southern Ocean where she collected rock samples from 300 sites, followed by intensive petrological and geochemical analyses at the GEOCHI. Based on the results she published series of articles in scientific magazines of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

properties.name: Morelli Ridge
properties.historia: Named after Prof. Carlo Morelli (1917-2007), an outstanding Earth Scientist and an enthusiastic supporter of GEBCO and Ocean Mapping. He studied in Pisa at the Regia Scuola Normale Superiore where he obtained a degree in Mathematics and in Physics in 1940 and got a University teaching qualification in Earth Physics in 1948. In 1949 he founded in Trieste the Osservatorio Geofisico Sperimentale (OGS) and was its Director until 1963 and its President until 1975. From 1971 to his death he was member of the Editorial Board for the International Bathymetric Chart of the Mediterranean (IBCM) and Vice-Chairman of the Consultation Group for Ocean Mapping (CGOM) of IOC. He led also to the compilation (for the IOC of UNESCO) first of the IBCM 1:1.000.000, published in 10 sheets in 1981, and later on (1985-99) of the Overlay Sheets with the gravity and magnetic anomalies, the seismicity and other geological and geophysical parameters. Carlo Morelli has achieved many scientific goals. The largest part of his experimental research is pertinent to Gravimetry. He proposed and led an endeavor which lasted for 20 years: the global gravity net and its standardization, which was officially adopted by the International Association of Geodesy at the Moscow 1971 General Assembly. This reference system (IGSN 71: International Gravity Standardization Net) represents also nowadays a basic instrument for the international cooperation and is universally adopted. Carlo Morelli is the author of 327 scientific papers (215 of which as the only author), mostly in international journals.

properties.name: Ferraz Peak
properties.historia:
Named after Luis Antônio de Carvalho Ferraz (1940-1982), a Brazilian Navy officer, engineer, hydrographer, oceanographer, and Brazilian pioneer in Antarctica. Commander Ferraz, participated in two expeditions in Antarctica on board British vessels RRS "Bransfield" and HMS "Endurance". He was instrumental in persuading the Brazilian government to establish a Brazilian Antarctic Program. 
He died on 11 August 1982, at the age of 42, while attending an oceanographic conference in Halifax, Canada, a few months before the first official Brazilian expedition in Antarctica took place. In recognition of his important role in preparing Brazil's Antarctic program, the Brazilian base in Antarctica has been named after him: Comandante Ferraz Brazilian Antarctic Base.

properties.name: Pirie Province
properties.historia: Named after Dr J. H. Harvey Pirie, a British versatile man of science and pioneer explorer of the Sub-Antarctic. Shortly after receiving a science and medical degree at Edinburgh, Dr Harvey Pirie joined the Scottish National Antarctic Expedition (1902-1904) on "S.Y. Scotia" under William S. Bruce. The naturalist team explored East Falkland, Laurie Island in the South Orkneys, and made the first oceanographic investigation of the Weddell Sea. After sighting Antarctica and naming the coast seen Coats Land, they returned to the Clyde via Gough Island and Cape Town. Dr. Pirie was the author of the expedition report "Zoological Log of Omond House, Scotia Bay". After a period in Scottish private practice, Pirie became a bacteriologist; he joined the Colonial Medical Service in 1913 and served in Kenya. In 1918 he organized the bacteriological services at the South African Institute for Medical Research in Johannesburg, and became deputy-director, 1926-1941.

properties.name: Sverdrup Canyon
properties.historia: Named after Harald Ulrik Sverdrup (1888 - 1957), a Norwegian oceanographer and meteorologist who made a number of important theoretical discoveries in these fields. He was director of the Scripps Institution of Oceanography (SIO, USA) from 1936 to 1948. During 33 expeditions with the research vessel "E. W. Scripps" in these years, he produced a detailed oceanographic dataset off the coast of California. He also developed a simple theory of the general ocean circulation postulating a dynamical vorticity balance between the wind-stress curl and the meridional gradient of the Coriolis parameter: the Sverdrup balance. He then returned home to become director of the Norwegian Polar Institute and continued to contribute to oceanography, ocean biology and polar research. His many publications include the magnum opus "The Oceans: Their Physics, Chemistry and General Biology" which formed the basic curriculum of oceanography for the next 40 years around the world. He was a member of the American and Norwegian Academies of Science and of the Swedish Order of the Polar Star. The sverdrup (Sv) is used in physical oceanography as an abbreviation for a volume flux of one million cubic meters per second. The American Meteorological Society named the Sverdrup Gold Medal Award in his honor as well.

properties.name: Paul Melchior Seamount
properties.historia: Named after Belgium Baron Paul Melchior (1926-2004). He contributed immensely to the development of geophysics not only as an outstanding scientist but also as a great leader. From 1973 to 1991, he served as Secretary General of International Union of Geodesy and Geophysics (IUGG) and was the Honorary Secretary General of IUGG until his death. His tenure lasted so long because he had an extraordinary ability to meet the expectations of his colleagues. One of his successes as Secretary General was the adhesion of China as member of IUGG, for which he showed all his skill in diplomatic matters. During his long and fruitful scientific career, Paul Melchior had been Director of the International Center for Earth Tides (1958-995), President of the Commission of Earth Rotation of the International Astronomical Union (1967-1970), and President of CODATA (1974-1978).

properties.name: Africana Rise
properties.historia: Named from the South African fisheries research vessel "Africana II" which worked extensively in this area in the 1960s.
properties.descubridor: South African fisheries research vessel "Africana II"

properties.name: Amundsen Abyssal Plain
properties.historia: Named after the Norwegian Polar explorer Roald Amundsen 1872-1928, who led the expedition that first reached the South Pole in 1911. He also was the first to fly over the North Pole on an airship in 1926.

properties.name: Belgica Guyot
properties.historia: Named from the research vessel "Belgica" of the Belgian Antarctic exploration cruise, 1896-1899, under the command of Lt. Adrien Victor Joseph de Gerlache (Royal Belgian Navy).
properties.proponente: Rick Hagen, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Bollons Seamount
properties.historia: Named after Captain J.P. Bollons, master of NZGS "Hinemoa" from 1898-1922 and who made a substantial contribution to New Zealand's early maritime history.

properties.name: Borchgrevink Trench
properties.historia: Named after the Anglo-Norwegian polar explorer Carsten Borchgrevink (1864-1934). He was the first to over-winter in the Antarctic.

properties.name: Enderby Abyssal Plain
properties.descubridor: Various vessels, notably British research vessel "Discovery II" and Russian research vessel "Ob"
properties.proponente: Marie Tharp and Bruce Heezen, Columbia University, USA

properties.name: Gallieni Rise
properties.historia: Named from the French supply vessel "Gallieni" that also made geophysical observations in 1960s - early 1970s in this area.
properties.proponente: Robert L. Fisher, Scripps Institution of Oceanography (SIO), USA

properties.name: Maurice Ewing Bank
properties.historia: Named after William Maurice "Doc" Ewing (1906-1974), a U.S. geophysicist and oceanographer, founding director of Lamont-Doherty Geological Observatory of Columbia University.

properties.name: Burdwood Bank
properties.historia: named in association with Burdwood Rock, a supposed navigational hazard reported by LT. T. Burdwood, agent for the "Kains" transport from Rio de Janeiro to Valparaiso (1828).

properties.name: Bounty Shelf
properties.historia: Named in association with the nearby Bounty Islands, which Lieutenant William Bligh, Commander of HMS Bounty, named after his ship in 1788.
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Cathedral Banks
properties.historia: Named for the spire-like appearance of the banks on the echo-sounding records.
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Papanui Canyon
properties.historia: Named in association with Papanui Inlet on the adjacent coast of New Zealand.
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Pickersgill Ridge
properties.historia: Named in association with Pickersgill Harbour, a natural harbour on the SW coast of the South Island of New Zealand, which Captain Cook used as an anchorage and named after Richard Pickersgill (1749-1779) of the HMS Resolution.
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Lena Seamount
properties.historia: Named from the Russian icebreaker research vessel "Lena" that discovered this feature when participating in the First Soviet Antarctic IGY Expedition.
properties.proponente: A. P. Lisitsyn, Institute of Oceanology of the Russian Academy of Sciences (IO RAS)

properties.name: Ob' Seamount
properties.historia: Named from the Russian research vessel "Ob" that discovered this feature.
properties.proponente: A. P. Lisitsyn, Institute of Oceanology of the Russian Academy of Sciences (IO RAS)

properties.name: Saunders Bank
properties.historia: Named in association with Saunders Coast, Antarctica.

properties.name: Weddell Abyssal Plain
properties.historia: Named after the  British sailor, navigator and seal hunter James Weddell (1787-1834), who discovered the Weddell Sea during his Antarctic voyage 1822-1824.

properties.name: Whales Bay Deeps
properties.historia: Named in association with Bay of Whales in Antarctica.

properties.name: Wordie Caldera
properties.historia: Named after James Wordie, who was the geologist on Ernest Shackleton's 1914 expedition to Antartica. They possibly drifted over this feature en route to Elephant Island.
properties.proponente: Stanley Robertson, Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences, Washington University in St. Louis, USA

properties.name: Palmer Basin
properties.historia: Named after the U.S. seaman Nathaniel B. Palmer (1799-1877), who was one of the discoverers of Palmer Peninsula, Antarctica. The feature is also close to Palmer Station, USA.
properties.proponente: Margaret Knuth, National Science Foundation, USA

properties.name: Polarstern Canyon
properties.historia: Named from the German research vessel "Polarstern", which carried out research work in the Weddell Sea from her first commissioning in 1982.
properties.proponente: Heinrich Hinze, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: Changcheng Seamount
properties.historia: Named from the Chinese Antarctic Great Wall station ("Changcheng" is the Chinese for "The Great Wall"), as this feature was the first seamount discovered by the Chinese research vessel "Xiang Yang Hong 1" on her way to the Great Wall station.
properties.proponente: The First Institute of Oceanography (SOA), China

properties.name: Beike Valley
properties.historia: Named from the nearby Beike Island, a small rock island close to the Chinese Antarctic Great Wall Station. The island was so named by the Chinese Antarctic Research Team in February 1986.
properties.proponente: China Geological Survey

properties.name: Zhenzhu Canyons
properties.historia: Named from the nearby Zhenzhu River, a small river close to the Antarctic Great Wall Station,a scientific station established by China. The river was named by the Chinese Antarctic Research Team in February 1986 and accepted by SCAR. "Zhenzhu" means "Pearl" in Chinese.
properties.proponente:
Guangzhou Marine Geological 
Survey, China

properties.name: Biyu Canyons
properties.historia: Named from the nearby Biyu Beach, close to the Antarctic Great Wall Station, a scientific station established by China. The beach was named by the Chinese Antarctic Research Team in 1986 and has been accepted by SCAR. "Biyu" means "Jade" in Chinese, a kind of precious stone.
properties.proponente: China Geological Survey

properties.name: Huangjin Ridge
properties.historia: Named from the nearby Huangjin Cove, close to the Chinese Antarctic Great Wall Station. The cove was so named by the Chinese Antarctic Research Team in February 1986.
properties.proponente: China Geological Survey

properties.name: Pacific-Antarctic Ridge
properties.historia: Named from its geographical position in the Southern part of the Pacific Ocean, close to Antarctica.

properties.name: Bligh Valley
properties.historia: Named after Lieutenant William Bligh, Commander of HMS Bounty, who discovered and named the adjacent Bounty islands in 1788.
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Endeavour Spur
properties.historia: Named from the New Zealand Antarctic supply vessel HMNZS "Endeavour".

properties.name: Haedal Seamounts
properties.historia: Named from its shape as this feature looks like a sea otter, "Haedal" in Korean.
properties.proponente: Korea Committee on Geographical Names (KCGN)

properties.name: Fiordland Trench
properties.historia: Named in association with Fiordland National Park on the adjacent mainland of the South Island of New Zealand.
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: North Bounty Channel
properties.historia: Named in association with the Bounty Islands, which Lieutenant William Bligh named after his ship HMS Bounty.
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: South Bounty Channel
properties.historia: Named in association with the Bounty Islands, which Lieutenant William Bligh named after his ship HMS "Bounty".
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Dolgae Hill
properties.historia: Named from its shape as various holes on this feature look like potholes, "Dolgae-gumung" in Korean.
properties.proponente: Korea Committee on Geographical Names (KCGN)

properties.name: A.R.A. San Juan Canyon
properties.historia: Named from the Argentinean Navy's Submarine A.R.A. "San Juan", lost on November 17th of 2017. The wreck was found at depth of 907 m on this feature on November 18th of 2018.
properties.proponente: Servicio de Hidrografía Naval, Argentina

properties.name: Ushuaia Seamount
properties.historia: Named from the nearby Argentinean city of Ushuaia, located at the southern tip of Argentina and capital of the Province of Tierra del Fuego. "Ushuaia" means "deep bay" in Yaghan, a native indigenous language of Tierra del Fuego.
properties.proponente: Servicio de Hidrografía Naval, Argentina

properties.name: Kurentsov Ridge
properties.historia: Named after the Russian entomologist, A. I. Kurentsov (1896-1975), who studied the Pacific region.
properties.proponente: Russian Federal Research Institute of Fisheries and Oceanography (VNIRO)

properties.name: Skif Seamount
properties.historia: Named from the Russian research vessel "Skif" that discovered this feature.
properties.proponente: Department of Navigation and Oceanography (DNO), Russia

properties.name: Aubert de la Rüe Seamounts
properties.historia: Named after Edgar Aubert de la Rüe (1901-1991), a noted French professor at the Musuem National d'Histoire Naturelle (Paris) and geologist who, between 1929 and 1967, published at least 27 papers on several aspects (petrology, sedimentology, glaciology) of the Kerguelen and Heard Islands.
properties.descubridor: French research and supply vessel "Marion Dufresne"
properties.proponente: Roland Schlich, Ecole et Observatoire de Physique du Globe (EOPG), France

properties.name: BANZARE Bank
properties.historia: Named after the British-Australian-New Zealand Antarctic Research Expedition (BANZARE), led by Sir Douglas Mawson, between 1929 and 1931.

properties.name: SANAE Bank
properties.historia: Named from the nearby South African research station SANAE (South African National Antarctic Expedition).
properties.proponente: Heinrich Hinze, Alfred-Wegener Institute for Polar and Marine Research (AWI), Germany

properties.name: SANAE Canyon
properties.historia: Named from the nearby South African research station SANAE (South African National Antarctic Expedition).

properties.name: Dotson-Getz Trough
properties.historia:
The trough is the extension from the Dotson and Getz Ice Shelves and
was likely be formed by ice streams extending from these ice shelves and
the connected glaciers.
properties.descubridor: Thomas B. Kellog, aboard U.S. icebreaker "Glacier"
properties.proponente: Frank O. Nitsche, Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory (L-DEO), Columbia University, USA

properties.name: El Austral Seamount
properties.historia: Named after the historical oceanographic sailing vessel "El Austral". Built in Copenhagen in 1935. she originally was the "Atlantis I" of Wood Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI). She was bought by the National Council of Scientific and Technical Research of Argentina in 1966. "El Austral" was also the name of a whaling ship, former polar explorer ship "Le Français" which belonged to the Argentinean Navy from 1905. The sailing vessel "El Austral" served with the Navy Hydrographic Service and carried out many scientific cruises in the Southwest Atlantic Ocean during the 1970´s. In 2012, she was owned by the Argentinean Naval Prefecture and used for fluvial and coastal environmental monitoring tasks.
properties.proponente: Walter Reynoso-Peralta, Argentinian Hydrographic Office (SHN)

properties.name: OGS Explora Mounds
properties.historia: Named after the Italian research vessel "OGS Explora", owned by the Istituto Nazionale di Oceanografia e di Geofisica Sperimentale (OGS). She went 10 times in the Antarctic seas and 6 times in the Ross Sea. The data collected during these cruises allowed to identify the mounds. This ship discovered similar features in the North Sea (Belgica Mounds, Logachev Mounds, Viking Mounds, etc.).
properties.proponente: Martina Busetti, National Institute of Oceanography and Experimental Geophysics (OGS),  Italy

properties.name: Pine Island Trough
properties.historia:
This feature is the extension from Pine Island Glacier and originates in Pine
Island Bay. It was most likely formed by the Pine Island Ice Stream.
The bay and the glacier are named after the ship "Pine Island", which
was part of the fleet that first reached Pine Island Bay.
properties.descubridor: Thomas B. Kellog, aboard U.S. icebreaker "Glacier"
properties.proponente: Frank O. Nitsche, Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory (L-DEO), Columbia University, USA

properties.name: South Orkney Plateau
properties.historia: Named from the nearby South Orkney Islands.
properties.proponente: Walter Reynoso-Peralta, Argentinian Hydrographic Office (SHN)

properties.name: Pūkākī Bank
properties.historia: Named after the New Zealand HMNZS "Pukaki" that surveyed this feature in 1950 (the correct orthography has macrons on the [u], [a] and [i]).
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Pūkākī Channel
properties.historia: Named after the nearby Pūkākī Bank, itself named from the New Zealand HMNZS "Pukaki" that surveyed the bank in 1950 (the correct orthography has macrons on the [u], [a] and [i]).

properties.name: Pūkākī Rise
properties.historia: Named from the New Zealand HMNZS "Pukaki" (the correct orthography has macrons on the [u], [a] and [i]).
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Pūkākī Saddle
properties.historia: Named from the New Zealand vessel HMNZS "Pukaki", which did research in this area (the correct orthography has macrons on the [u], [a] and [i]).
properties.proponente: Mark Dyer, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB); and Adam Greenland, New Zealand Hydrographic Office (LINZ)

properties.name: Karitāne Canyon
properties.historia: Named from the Karitāne settlement on the adjacent mainland.
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Karitāne Channel
properties.historia: Named from the Karitāne settlement on the adjacent mainland, New Zealand (the correct orthography has a macron on the 2nd [a]).
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Boongorang Canyons
properties.historia: Boongorang means “blowing in the wind” in the language of the Noongar people who are the indigenous people of the part of Australia that was adjacent to the Sabrina Coast before continental break up and drift. The name was chosen because this feature was mapped while bad weather delayed planned activities.
properties.proponente: Ph.E. O’Brien, Macquarie University, Sydney, Australia; and L. Armand, Australian National University, Canberra, Australia

properties.name: Manang Canyons
properties.historia: Manang means “pool of water” in the language of the Noongar people who are the indigenous people of the part of Australia that was adjacent to the Sabrina Coast before continental break up and drift. The name was chosen because canyons in the area have sections of reverse gradient known as scour pools which would form pools of water in a river.
properties.proponente: Ph.E. O’Brien, Macquarie University, Sydney, Australia; and L. Armand, Australian National University, Canberra, Australia

properties.name: Morka Valley
properties.historia: Morka means winter in the language of the Noongar people who are the indigenous people of the part of Australia that was adjacent to the Sabrina Coast before continental break up and drift. The valley is thought to only receive currents and sediment from the continent during ice ages.
properties.proponente: Ph.E. O’Brien, Macquarie University, Sydney, Australia; and L. Armand, Australian National University, Canberra, Australia

properties.name: Minang-a Canyon
properties.historia: Minang-a means whale in the language of the Noongar people who are the indigenous people of the part of Australia that was adjacent to the Sabrina Coast before continental break up and drift. The survey encountered many whales in the area.
properties.proponente: Ph.E. O’Brien, Macquarie University, Sydney, Australia; and L. Armand, Australian National University, Canberra, Australia

properties.name: Maadjit Canyons
properties.historia: Maadjit means water snake in the language of the Noongar people who are the indigenous people of the part of Australia that was adjacent to the Sabrina Coast before continental break up and drift. The name was chosen because of the sinuous tributary canyons which are unusually curved (snake-like) for this area.
properties.proponente: Ph.E. O’Brien, Macquarie University, Sydney, Australia; and L. Armand, Australian National University, Canberra, Australia

properties.name: Jeffrey Canyons
properties.historia: Named after the Australian scientist Dr. Shirley Jeffrey (1930-2014), a preeminent researcher in the biochemistry of phytoplankton. This feature was chosen because its floor contains unexpected thick deposits of phytoplankton (diatoms).
properties.proponente: Ph.E. O’Brien, Macquarie University, Sydney, Australia; and L. Armand, Australian National University, Canberra, Australia

properties.name: Elan Bank
properties.historia: Named after Professor Hayes’s step-daughter Elan.
properties.proponente: Dennis E. Hayes, Lamont-Doherty Geological Observatory (L-DGO), Columbia University, USA

properties.name: Orionids Seamount
properties.historia: Named in relation to the German research vessel ‘Meteor’ that discovered and surveyed the South Sandwich Trench. Orionids is the name of a Meteor shower.
properties.proponente: A. Jamieson & C. Bongiovanni, Newcastle University, UK

properties.name: Nova Ridge
properties.historia: Named in relation to the German research vessel ‘Meteor’ that discovered and surveyed the South Sandwich Trench. A nova is a transient astronomical event that causes the sudden appearance of a bright, apparently "new" star, that slowly fades over several weeks or many months.
properties.proponente: A. Jamieson & C. Bongiovanni, Newcastle University, UK

properties.name: Aquariids Deep
properties.historia: Named in relation to the German research vessel ‘Meteor’ that discovered and surveyed the South Sandwich Trench. Aquariids is the name of a Meteor shower.
properties.proponente: A. Jamieson & C. Bongiovanni, Newcastle University, UK

properties.name: Bitter Deep
properties.historia: Named in relation to the bad whether conditions, and its consequences, that the ship and scientific party encountered during the month long voyage to the South Sandwich Trench. It was on this site where the majority of bad luck occurred and led to the loss of a lot of equipment.
properties.proponente: A. Jamieson & C. Bongiovanni, Newcastle University, UK

properties.name: Factorian Deep
properties.historia: Named in relation to the full ocean depth submersible ‘Limiting Factor’ that successfully reached the bottom of this feature, deepest point in the Southern Ocean.
properties.proponente: A. Jamieson & C. Bongiovanni, Newcastle University, UK

properties.name: Frozen Hill
properties.historia: Named in relation to the extreme whether conditions that the expedition had to endure to survey and discover this feature.
properties.proponente: A. Jamieson & C. Bongiovanni, Newcastle University, UK

properties.name: Hydris Deep
properties.historia: Named in relation to the German research vessel ‘Meteor’ that discovered and surveyed the South Sandwich Trench. Hydris is the name of a Meteor shower.
properties.proponente: A. Jamieson & C. Bongiovanni, Newcastle University, UK

properties.name: Leonids Deep
properties.historia: Named in relation to the German research vessel ‘Meteor’ that discovered and surveyed the South Sandwich Trench. Leonids is the name of a Meteor shower.
properties.proponente: A. Jamieson & C. Bongiovanni, Newcastle University, UK

properties.name: Limiting Deep
properties.historia: Named in relation to the full ocean depth submersible ‘Limiting Factor’ that successfully reached the bottom of this feature, second deepest point in the Southern Ocean.
properties.proponente: A. Jamieson & C. Bongiovanni, Newcastle University, UK

properties.name: Perseids Deep
properties.historia: Named in relation to the German research vessel ‘Meteor’ that discovered and surveyed the South Sandwich Trench. Perseids is the name of a Meteor shower.
properties.proponente: A. Jamieson & C. Bongiovanni, Newcastle University, UK

properties.name: Princess Elizabeth Trough
properties.historia: Named after Professor Hayes’s daughter Elizabeth (Libby).
properties.proponente: Dennis E. Hayes, Lamont-Doherty Geological Observatory (L-DGO), Columbia University, USA

properties.name: Pegasus Ridge
properties.historia: Named from 'Pegasus', a mythical winged divine horse, and one of the most recognized creatures in Greek mythology. Usually depicted as pure white (like Antarctica), 'Pegasus' is the offspring of the Olympian god of the sea 'Poseidon'.
properties.proponente: A. Jamieson & C. Bongiovanni, Newcastle University, UK

properties.name: Farr Knoll
properties.historia: Named after Clinton Coleridge Farr (1866-1943), who made a meaningful contribution to ocean science as a member of New Zealand’s 1907 Sub-Antarctic Islands Scientific Expedition.
properties.proponente: A. Haanen, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Ice Bird Peak
properties.historia: "Ice Bird" commemorates the name of the yacht in which David Henry Lewis (1917-2002), a Polynesian scholar and an expert in traditional Polynesian navigation, is reputed to have made the first single-handed circumnavigation of Antarctica.
properties.proponente: A. Haanen, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Kidson Hills
properties.historia: Named after Dr Edward Kidson (1882-1939), who was an authority on Antarctic meteorology and who made a meaningful contribution to ocean science as a member of New Zealand’s 1907 Sub-Antarctic Islands Scientific Expedition.
properties.proponente: A. Haanen, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Leachman Hill
properties.historia: Named after Andrew Leachman (1945-2017), who was Master of the New Zealand research vessels "James Cook" and "Tangaroa". His time in command of these two vessels saw him operate extensively around New Zealand and in the Antarctic waters of the Southern Ocean in support of significant national and international marine research programmes.
properties.proponente: A. Haanen, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Pelorus Ridge
properties.historia: Named for and commemorates New Zealand’s National Institute of Water and Atmospheric Research’s (NIWA) small swath bathymetry research vessel "Pelorus" that undertook a hydrographic survey of the nearby seabed adjacent to Cape Adare, Antarctica.
properties.proponente: A. Haanen, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Solo Peak
properties.historia: "Solo" commemorates the name of the yacht that David Henry Lewis (1917-2002), who was an expert in traditional Polynesian navigation, captained on a scientific expedition to Antarctica in 1977-78.
properties.proponente: A. Haanen, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Wintery Deep
properties.historia: Named in relation to the extreme winter-like conditions that the expedition had to endure to survey and discover this feature.
properties.proponente: A. Jamieson & C. Bongiovanni, Newcastle University, UK

properties.name: Meteor North Hill
properties.historia: Named from the German exploration vessel "Meteor" and also from the nearby Meteor Rise.
properties.proponente: Caladan Oceanic LLC, Texas, USA

properties.name: Vysokaya Bank
properties.historia: Named from the shape of this feature; "Vysok" means "head" or "temple" in Russian. Vysokaya (Vysokaja) also means ‘high’ in Russian.
properties.proponente: Russian Federal Research Institute of Fisheries and Oceanography (VNIRO)

properties.name: William Benham Seamount
properties.historia: Named after William Blaxland Benham (1860–1950). His large body of scientific work included publications on the sub-Antarctic islands and material collected on Scott’s Antarctic expedition (1910-1913). The first name (William) is included to avoid duplication with a ‘Benham’ feature in the Philippine Sea, named after the captain of the vessel who discovered it.
properties.proponente: A. Haanen, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Aho Ridge
properties.historia: Aho is the Māori word for a fishing line, and the feature is adjacent to the seamount named Upokororo (a fish).
properties.proponente: A. Haanen, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Chilton Hill
properties.historia: Named after Charles Chilton (1860-1929), who made a meaningful contribution to ocean science as a member of New Zealand’s 1907 Sub-Antarctic Islands Scientific Expedition.
properties.proponente: A. Haanen, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Herriott Hill
properties.historia: Named after Elizabeth Maude Herriott (1882-1936), a New Zealand scientist and academic who made a meaningful contribution to ocean science by undertaking a pioneering study of the giant kelp Durvillea Antarctica.
properties.proponente: A. Haanen, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: KOPRI Seamount
properties.historia: Named for the Korea Polar Research Institute (KOPRI) which discovered this feature.
properties.proponente: Korea Committee on Geographical Names (KCGN)

properties.name: Kūmara Hill
properties.historia: Named from its shape as this feature resembles a kūmara (sweet potato, in Māori language).
properties.proponente: A. Haanen, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Laing Hill
properties.historia: Named after Robert Malcolm Laing (1865-1941), who made a meaningful contribution to ocean science as a member of New Zealand’s 1907 Sub-Antarctic Islands Scientific Expedition. His biological work described various seaweeds.
properties.proponente: A. Haanen, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Meteor Deep
properties.historia: Named from the German research vessel "Meteor" that discovered and surveyed the South Sandwich Trench, including this feature.
properties.proponente: A. Jamieson & C. Bongiovanni, Newcastle University, UK

properties.name: Piloto Pardo Seamount
properties.historia: Named from the Chilean Navy officer, Second Pilot Luis Pardo Villalón (Piloto Pardo, in Spanish), who led in 1916 the heroic rescue of the crew of Sir Ernest Schackleton´s expedition on brig “Endurance”, wrecked in Antarctica. Pilot Pardo, in command of the fragile Chilean vessel “Yelcho”, successfully overcame the icy and turbulent waters of the southern seas to recover alive all the shipwrecked Englishmen from the Antarctic territory. The feat of Pilot Pardo, which occurred near this geographical feature, is a remarkable nautical event that is highlighted and admired by the world to this day.
properties.proponente: Hydrographic and Oceanographic Office  of the Chilean Navy (SHOA)

properties.name: Pōhā Hill
properties.historia: Named from its shape as this feature resembles a pōhā, which is the Māori word for a receptacle made of rimurapa (kelp) and tōtara bark, and used to hold preserved birds and fish.
properties.proponente: A. Haanen, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Pohau Hill
properties.historia: Named from its shape as this feature resembles a pohau, which is the Māori word for a large wooden fishing hook with a bone barb.
properties.proponente: A. Haanen, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Sars Guyot
properties.historia:
Named after the eminent, world-renowned Norwegian marine scientists, father and son Michael and Georg Ossian Sars, who are regarded as
pioneers in marine research.
properties.proponente: Royal Norwegian Society for Sciences, Trondheim, Norway

properties.name: Skey Hill
properties.historia: Named after Henry Fawsit Skey (1877-1947), who made a meaningful contribution to ocean science as a member of New Zealand’s 1907 Sub-Antarctic Islands Scientific Expedition.
properties.proponente: A. Haanen, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Tuaki Hill
properties.historia: Named from its shape as this feature resembles a tuaki, which is the southern tribal dialect (Ngāi Tahu) for 'tuangi', the New Zealand cockle.
properties.proponente: A. Haanen, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Upokororo Seamount
properties.historia: Upokororo is the Māori name of an extinct fish native to New Zealand, and the feature is adjacent to the ridge named Aho (a fishing line).
properties.proponente: A. Haanen, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Aurora Bank
properties.historia: Named from the Australian research vessel "Aurora Australis" which did a great deal of work on the fisheries, marine biology, oceanography and bathymetry of the Heard Island plateau during 1990-1993. The name also recognizes the marine scientific work of the Steam Yacht "Aurora" on the Australian Antarctic Expedition and Shackleton's 1914 expedition.
properties.proponente: J. J. Doyle, Australian Hydrographic Service (AHS)

properties.name: Campbell Island / Motu Ihupuku Shelf
properties.historia: Named from the nearby Campbell Island ("Motu Ihupuku" in Maori language), New Zealand. This dual name reflects that of the associated land feature, Campbell Island / Motu Ihupuku, which was made official in the New Zealand Ngai Tahu Claims Settlement Act 1998.
properties.proponente: Mark Dyer, New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB); and Adam Greenland, New Zealand Hydrographic Office (LINZ)

properties.name: Petrov Seamount
properties.historia: Named after Andrey Vasilyevich Petrov (1927-1974), a Russian hydrographer who served in hydrographic subdivisions of the Pacific Fleet. He participated in hydrographic researchs in the Far East seas and was involved in the development of technical aids of the World Ocean study and exploitation.
properties.proponente: Department of Navigation and Oceanography (DNO), Russia

properties.name: Nasyr' Seamount
properties.historia: Named after Leonid Petrovich Nasyr' (1924-2003), a Russian hydrographer who served in hydrographic subdivisions of the Pacific Fleet. He contributed to the complex oceanographic study of the Far East seas, including Kuril'skiye Ostrova. He was involved in the establishment and organization of the chart production at the Pacific Fleet.
properties.proponente: Department of Navigation and Oceanography (DNO), Russia

properties.name: Elcano Rise
properties.historia: Named after Juan Sebastian Elcano (1476-1526), a Spanish pilot sailing with Ferdinand Magellan, who brought the Victoria back to Portugal following the death of Magellan. The ship passed near this feature before rounding Cape of Good Hope and completing the first circumnavigation of the globe (1519-1522).
properties.proponente: Robert L. Fisher, Scripps Institution of Oceanography (SIO), USA

properties.name: Adare Sea Channel
properties.historia: Named in association with the land feature, Cape Adare, which itself was named by Captain James Ross (1800-1862) for his friend Viscount Adare (1812-1861), Member of Parliament for Glamorganshire, England.
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Wilson Canyon
properties.historia: Named after Dr. Edward Wilson, medical officer on Scott's expeditions. A key member of Scott's Last Expedition. Died with Scott in 1913.

properties.name: Waite Hills
properties.historia: Named after Edgar Waite (1866-1928) a leading ichthyologist and member of the 1911 Australasian Antarctic Expedition. He took soundings and did dredging between Tasmania and Antarctica. A major work of Waite was 'Fishes of the Australasian Antarctic Expedition' (1916), a domain where he was a world authority.
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Veryan Valley
properties.historia: Named from the British HMS "Veryan Bay", which took soundings in the area in 1950.
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Christoffel Hill
properties.historia: Named after New Zealand geophysicist David Christoffel (1929-2014), in recognition of his work in the Southern Ocean and Antarctica.
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Taumoana Canyon
properties.historia: First appeared as Five Fingers Canyon on Coastal Bathymetry Series (CBS) chart 'Dusky' in 2001. Altered to Taumoana Canyon to restore the original Māori name of the associated land feature, Five Fingers Peninsula. "Taumoana" means 'one of the islands on which Tū stood as he strained to lengthen the sounds'. The associated marine reserve is also named Taumoana (Five Finger Peninsula) Marine Reserve.
properties.proponente: New Zealand Geographic Board (NZGB)

properties.name: Huangmei Ridge
properties.historia: Named from the yellow browed penguin, "Huangmei" in Chinese ("huang" means "yellow"), which is widely distributed in this area.  The feature shaped curve,resembles the eyebrow of this penguin,
properties.proponente: National Marine Data and Information Service (NMDIS), China

properties.name: Jintu Hill
properties.historia: Named from the Gentoo penguin, "Jintu" in Chinese, which is widely distributed in this area.
properties.proponente: National Marine Data and Information Service (NMDIS), China

properties.name: Barker Plateau
properties.historia: Named after Peter F. Barker (1939-2012) who wrote extensively on the tectonics of the Scotia Sea and mapped this feature; see Cunningham et al., 1996; Barker, 2001.
properties.proponente: Lawrence L. Lawver and Ian W. D. Dalziel, University of Texas at Austin, USA;  and Robert Larter, British Antarctic Survey (BAS)

properties.name: Maodai Hill
properties.historia:
Maodai means "chinstrap" in Chinese language. Chinstrap penguins are
widely distributed in this area.
properties.proponente: National Marine Data and Information Service (NMDIS), China

properties.name: Vidal Gormaz Seamount
properties.historia: Named after the Chilean Navy Captain Francisco Vidal Gormaz (1837-1907), a pioneer in hydrographic explorations in the country, carrying out several campaigns and studies in the areas of Hydrography, Geography, Meteorology, and Astronomy, among other related sciences. He was the first Director of the Hydrographic Office of Chile. He is considered the father of national hydrography.
properties.proponente: Hydrographic and Oceanographic Office  of the Chilean Navy (SHOA)

properties.name: Sejong Seamount
properties.historia: Named from the King Sejong Station, South Korea's Antarctic research base. This station serves as a vital hub for Korean scientists conducting diverse research in the Antarctic region. The station itself was named after King Sejong the Great, the revered fourth monarch of the Joseon Dynasty in Korean history.
properties.proponente: Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (KHOA)

properties.name: KHOA Seamount
properties.historia: Named from the Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (KHOA) that discovered this feature with the Korean icebreaker and research vessel "Araon", where their researchers acquired and processed the bathymetric data.
properties.proponente: Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (KHOA)

properties.name: Araon Hill
properties.historia: Named from the Korea Polar Research Institute's icebreaking research vessel "Araon". Most of the undersea features that Korea discovered in the Antarctic region were found by the R/V "Araon".
properties.proponente: Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (KHOA)

properties.name: Sokuri Knoll
properties.historia: Named from its shape as the feature ressembles a “Sokuri”, a traditional Korean woven basket made from thin bamboo or straw. It has a round, shallow, and slightly convex shape, historically used to carry or dry grains, vegetables, or seafood. It is a culturally significant item, commonly found in Korean rural and coastal life.
properties.proponente: Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency (KHOA)
